result.title: Fisher information and the geometry of memorization in neural networks
result.comment: 20 pages (10 pages main text), 11 figures (6 figures main text), NeurIPS 2026
result.summary: A fruitful approach towards understanding generalization in machine learning involves characterizing how models separate generalizable structure from idiosyncratic or even corrupted features of training data. Fisher information has emerged as a diagnostic tool for this separation, leveraging loss geometry to distinguish generalization from memorization. Here we investigate this connection in vision models trained on CIFAR-10 with controlled noise that can be learned only through memorization. We show that projecting model weights onto the top Fisher eigenvectors decouples general task performance from noisy sample memorization, and we investigate how this decoupling presents differentially across layers. We show that the same phenomena are present in small transformers trained to solve a synthetic in-context learning task, and are reproduced in closed form in a simple, analytically solvable linear model. Our results reveal that Fisher information captures aspects of the geometric structure underlying how neural networks allocate capacity between generalization and memorization.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在 CIFAR-10 加可控噪声的视觉模型上考察 Fisher 信息作为区分泛化与记忆的诊断工具，发现把权重投影到 top Fisher 特征向量可使通用任务性能与噪声样本记忆解耦，并比较该解耦在不同层间的差异，另在小型 transformer 的合成 in-context 学习任务与可解析线性模型中复现同类现象。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「用损失/表示几何区分可泛化结构与样本特异噪声」的分析视角，可能可供核查用于判断 latent 状态中保留的是任务必要视觉信息还是记忆成分，并与关注 latent 相似度中内容、深度、缓存结构差异的问题表述相关。
